newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SKODA SAYS WINS $62MLN YUGOSLAVIA POWER DEAL.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SKODA SAYS WINS $62MLN YUGOSLAVIA POWER DEAL.

text.p: Czech engineering concern Skoda a.s. said on Tuesday it had signed a $62 million contract with Yugoslav power generator EPS for equipment supplies to Yugoslavia's 700 megawatt power plant, Kolubara B.
The company said in a statement that the supplies would be financed by Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s., the Czech Export Bank and the Czech government insurance company EGAP.
"This is the first stage of completion of two 350 megawatt blocs, which includes supplies of steel constructions, generators and transformers," Skoda statement said.
Skoda said it would begin supplies in the third quarter of this year with the help of some local companies.
The company said it was aiming to win a further $38 million contract for the second stage of the power plant's completion.
"Negotiations are continuing intensively," the statement said.
Kolubara B is due to open between 2000 and 2001.
Skoda, based in the western Czech city of Plzen, has been a traditional supplier of power generating equipment to the territory of former Yugoslavia.
Business was interrupted because of the war in the former Yugoslavia and the subsequent trade embargo.
